introduction: Read the RSA arithmetic companion in the written lab. The eight worked sources expose individual arithmetic boundaries, then the staged checks build seven reusable interfaces in one independent source. Predictions are inline in MARS Learning. Finish each Debug process before another launch or source edit.
conclusion: Explain how limb width, carry and reduced residues fit together. Trace a full-width exponent bit across a limb boundary, distinguish gcd value from status, and defend zero-modulus access precedence. Use the final full recheck after implementation edits and investigate an additional input of your own.

steps.explanation: The first unsigned division has produced 13 mod 11 = 2. Euclid replaces A,B by B,remainder; both replacements must use the old values.
steps.question: Which pair should the next division use?

choices.feedback: The common divisors are unchanged, and the second operand has decreased.

steps.explanation: The same 64 bits can denote unsigned 18446744073709551615 or signed -1. The gcd interface specifies the unsigned interpretation.
steps.question: Which remainder does unsigned division of ffffffffffffffff by 17 produce?

choices.feedback: That is the signed remainder; its all-one bit pattern is not an unsigned residue below 17.
2^64-1 is divisible by 17. The signed remainder of -1 is a different operation.
That is the least nonnegative residue of signed -1, not of the specified unsigned dividend.

steps.explanation: The complete product of two maximum unsigned words is fffffffe00000001. Its low word alone is one. Its signed doubleword interpretation is negative.
steps.question: Which operation reduces the complete product according to the unsigned interface?

choices.feedback: Retain all 64 product bits until reduction. A 32-bit divisor does not imply a 32-bit dividend.

choices.text: A remainder of the low word only
choices.feedback: Discarding the high product bits changes the dividend.

steps.explanation: One addition column contains two unsigned 32-bit limbs and an incoming carry of one. The complete sum is 1ffffffff.
steps.question: Which low limb and outgoing carry should be retained?

choices.feedback: Dropping the carry loses the contribution at the next limb position.
The low 32 bits become this column; the remaining bit moves to the next column.

steps.explanation: Four 32-bit limbs describe one unsigned 128-bit input. A full product must retain its high half even when a later modular operation would discard it.
steps.question: How much output can the full product of two such inputs require?

choices.feedback: That would retain only the low half of some products.
